apps.verdict: A visually polished budget planner with multiple accounts, credit cards, and goals. Claims cross-device sync and bank connections, but that is exactly where everything breaks: balance differs between phone and web, data disappears, and part of the interface appears in Portuguese. The app is Brazilian in origin and is roughly implemented for English-speaking users.
apps.loved: A visual dashboard with goal progress and payment reminders appeals to those who manage to get it working.
apps.weak: Cross-device sync does not work: balances diverge. Several months of history disappear after reinstallation. The interface switches to Portuguese. No balance forecast.
apps.whoFor: Practically no one at this point: too many systemic failures for everyday financial tracking.

apps.title: Belco Money Manager
apps.verdict: The Belco credit union mobile banking app, not an independent financial management tool. A significant portion of users cannot log in, have lost transfer features, or face repeated authentication errors. The high rating reflects customer loyalty to the credit union itself, not to the app.
apps.loved: Fast balance check via biometrics when it works. Loyal union members value convenient access to familiar operations.
apps.weak: Authentication breaks when switching networks. Updates regularly disable transfer features that were working. Balance does not update in real time after transactions. No budgeting functionality at all.
apps.whoFor: Belco Credit Union members exclusively who need basic mobile access to their account.

apps.title: Budget – Car Rental
apps.verdict: The Budget Car Rental app lets you book and manage reservations, but it is a rental service storefront, not a personal finance management tool. In a financial control context it is useless: it does not help understand expenses, shows no budget, and keeps no spending history. Separately: the rental service itself receives many complaints about undisclosed add-on charges.
apps.loved: Booking and viewing reservation details works without extra steps. The Fastbreak loyalty program displays correctly.
apps.weak: The app does not automatically sync reservations after login and does not remember saved data. No transparent display of the final amount before handing over the keys. Rental history over several years is stored unreliably.
apps.whoFor: For managing Budget Car Rental reservations only. Not applicable as a financial tool.

apps.title: Dollarwise: Budget & Tracking
apps.verdict: An app with automatic bank sync and spending categorization. The concept is modern, but execution is rough: transactions duplicate, categories reset, and account connections freeze. Several rounds of overhauls have not resolved the underlying issues.
apps.loved: The concept of automatic sync and a clean overview of all accounts in one place appeals to those tired of manual entry. The visual design is modern and pleasant.
apps.weak: Transactions duplicate and fail to bind to categories. Categories reset. Support does not respond for weeks. No way to disconnect an account and export data.
apps.whoFor: Fans of the Financial Audit podcast willing to risk a subscription in hopes of the next update.

apps.title: Pocket Expense 6
apps.verdict: The app was a popular manual expense register for more than ten years. In 2024-2025, several updates wiped data for users with years of history. The developer stopped responding to requests. The company website is offline.
apps.loved: In its prime. a simple and clear spending log without bank integration. The discipline of manual entry was valued by users.
apps.weak: The 2024-2025 update deleted transaction history for users with years of data. Sync on a new device freezes and does not complete. Support does not respond. The website is down.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone at this point. If data has not yet been lost, export it immediately.

apps.title: Receipt Scanner・Track Expenses
apps.verdict: Claims receipt scanning and report generation for expense reimbursement. In practice: OCR assigns the wrong date, the app loses uploaded receipts, and reports either fail to generate or produce a blank page.
apps.loved: The idea of instantly scanning a receipt and getting a ready report for accounting theoretically saves hours. Fast image capture.
apps.weak: Receipts are lost after updates. OCR assigns the wrong date almost every time. Reports fail to generate or produce a blank page. History cannot be viewed without extended access.
apps.whoFor: No one: the app does not perform its core function reliably enough for real-world use.

apps.title: Costpoint Time and Expense
apps.verdict: A corporate tool for timesheet and travel expense tracking, imposed on contractor employees by employers. Users are unanimous: constant session drops, lost entered data, and an archaic interface make daily timesheet entry an ordeal. Not applicable as a personal finance tool at all.
apps.loved: The only upside: the ability to submit a timesheet from a phone without opening a laptop, when the app does not crash.
apps.weak: The session drops several times a day, taking unsaved data with it. No proper PIN login. The interface has not been updated in years and requires training for basic actions.
apps.whoFor: Exclusively employees of companies where Costpoint has been selected corporately, with no alternative available.

apps.title: Budget Planner: Budget, Bills
apps.verdict: The app collects income and expense data, then locks access to it without warning. Basic functionality such as month-over-month comparison and history editing is absent even with extended access.
apps.loved: A clear remaining-budget screen is convenient at a glance. Fast expense category setup at the start.
apps.weak: Data entered during setup disappears behind a paywall without warning. Past months cannot be viewed or edited. Constant pop-up requests appear every 45 seconds.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in its current state.

apps.title: BuyBye - Budget Planner
apps.verdict: The concept of converting a price into work hours is interesting as an awareness tool, but the implementation amounts to simple division. There is no expense management, no forecasts, and no history.
apps.loved: The idea of converting a price into work hours creates a psychological pause before an impulse purchase.
apps.weak: All functionality is locked without extended access. A rating request appears before the user has tried anything. Functionality amounts to a single formula that any calculator provides for free.
apps.whoFor: No one. Any calculator solves this problem for free.

apps.title: Kiplinger Personal Finance
apps.verdict: This is a digital magazine reader, not a financial app. Its only function is to read downloaded issues. Most users cannot even log in: web access credentials are not recognized by the app. Support does not respond.
apps.loved: The magazine content is considered useful by the rare users for whom login did work. The familiar magazine article format on personal finance topics.
apps.weak: Login does not work for most users. Web subscription credentials are not recognized in the app. Issue history disappears after updates. No working user support.
apps.whoFor: No one, until login and subscription integration issues are resolved.

scenarios.name: People who track spending by hand
scenarios.job: Keep a detailed record of every purchase by hand, build a personal financial archive over years, and never give third-party services access to the bank account.
scenarios.gap: Entering things by hand is useful for people who want to notice every purchase. Fast entry, a category that makes sense and the ability to keep an archive of one’s own all matter.

scenarios.name: People planning their spending until the next income
scenarios.job: Get one safe figure for each day, so as not to spend too much at the start of the month and not to run out by the end.
scenarios.gap: It has to be clear which bills are already accounted for in the available amount and how it will change before the next income. An opaque formula forces a person to recalculate everything themselves.

scenarios.name: Couples who run a shared budget in different ways
scenarios.job: One partner keeps the budget, the other wants to know one figure and not to fight about money.
scenarios.gap: One partner may keep detailed records while the other needs the overall balance. It helps to separate personal money from shared money, the roles, and the level of visibility.

scenarios.name: A person with ADHD or impulsive spending
scenarios.job: Hold on to a money habit thanks to the simplest possible interface and one clear metric that needs no decoding.
scenarios.gap: Reviews from this group value a balance that is clear and a small amount of daily work. A game, simple entry and setting money aside automatically are different forms of support, not mutually exclusive rules for everyone.

scenarios.name: A follower of the cashless envelope method
scenarios.job: Apply the Ramsey method digitally: allocate income to categories in advance and spend only from an envelope, without giving bank access.
scenarios.gap: Money is allocated to a purpose in advance and they want to see how much is left in each envelope. Separately, a person’s attitude to the cloud, to bank access and to running it jointly has to be understood.
